title: Heuristic threads and blindspots - Ryden Han
content:
Purpose: quick, messy brain dump after Ryden's onscreen loop. Use as raw feed for panel and hiring manager; this is not polished.

Context notes to self:
- Role: Senior Runtime Engineer (latency/cost/kv-kv caching/quantization familiarity expected).
- Interview format: 60m loop — system design (30m), troubleshooting/coding (20m), behavioral (10m).
- Candidate background: MLOps + infra at midsize startup; implemented custom caching layer for transformer caching in production; some PyTorch C++ kernel work but not full time. Said they shipped quantized models but unclear on toolchain.

High-level gut summary (2-sentence):
- Strong product-systems thinker who maps trade-offs calmly; comfortable with SRE/infra processes. Could be solid IC for Dedicated capacity optimizations but may need pairing on low-level kernel work.
- Main risk: possibility of over-indexing on engineering pragmatism and not enough depth on GPU kernel internals / compiler-level perf hacks we use.

Concrete strengths I noticed:
- Thoughtful about measurement: kept asking what metric exactly we optimize for (p50 vs p99 vs cost/token) and suggested concrete tests. Good sign of pragmatic instrumentation mindset.
- Evokes real-world constraints: caching invalidation, multi-tenant fairness, warmup stalls. Proposed a sensible backoff for cache-thrashing.
- Ops experience: wrote good runbook-oriented answers — how to triage step-by-step and which alerts to attach to a regression.
- Communicated trade-offs clearly rather than parroting academic optimizations.

Weaknesses / blindspots:
- Kernel/compilation depth: when pushed on fused-kernel tradeoffs (fp16 attenuation, attention unrolling), answer was handwavy and referenced collaborators rather than specifics. Could be fine if we pair with infra-compiler folks, but not a solo kernel owner.
- Sparse quantization toolchain knowledge: said they used "off-the-shelf" but couldn't explain calibration steps or per-layer quantization decisions for LLMs.
- A bit conservative on risk — default to safer, simpler deployments. For early-stage optimization work (we sometimes need aggressive experimentation), might be slower to prototype.

Behavioral signals:
- Team fit: calm, low-loudness, listens. Good candidate for cross-team troubleshooting and on-call rotations.
- Ownership: gave examples of owning incidents end-to-end, included follow-ups and postmortem steps — seems mature.

Probing questions I wish I'd asked / follow-ups for next loop:
- Ask for a specific NUMA-aware allocation strategy they implemented and the measured impact (numbers, before/after).
- Have them whiteboard the memory layout for KV-cache entries and eviction policy when entries have variable-length kvs — ask to sketch amortized cost of lookup under 95th percentile load.
- Request a concrete quantization failure mode they observed in prod and how they detected it (metrics/inputs).

Suggested score (quick heuristic):
- Technical depth: 6/10 (strong infra/system design, weaker kernel/compilation)
- Operability / SRE: 8/10
- Role fit (senior IC for Dedicated/Private deployments): 7/10
- Recommendation: move to hiring manager review / paired session with kernel/quant expert before final decision.

Red flags (if any):
- None immediate. Watch for: inability to give numbers when asked; if follow-up reveals no hands-on quantization steps, then that becomes a material risk for projects needing quantization expertise.

Suggested next steps (for team):
- Short technical follow-up: 30m pairing session with someone from applied-ml or serving-runtime (Marcus or Aisha) focused on a concrete kernel/quantization problem. Keep it narrow: e.g., "explain the quantization calibration you ran and walk through a failing case."
- Ops check: give them an on-call incident scenario and see how they prioritize mitigations vs long-term fixes. 20–30m.
- If follow-up passes, propose an offer band aligned with senior IC (level depends on compensation comp table) — but prefer to de-risk kernel gap with hiring/mentor plan.

Notes to hiring manager (short):
- Good fit for Dedicated capacity and cross-team reliability; will excel in shipping robust infra and runbooks. Not our strongest candidate for kernel/compiler specialist roles. Recommend follow-up pair session with kernel owner before final yes.

Random scratch items I scribbled during interview (raw):
- "p50 cost per token vs p99 latency tradeoff" phrase used 3x — candidate thinks about cost ops.
- Mentioned a "fused attention microkernel" but couldn't show perf numbers.
- Likes canary traffic splits + layered fallbacks.

Decision leaning: continue (de-risk with targeted follow-ups).

End of dump.

-- Samir
